paper.title: A Sharp Memory-Regret Trade-Off for Multi-Pass Streaming Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Limited memory multi-pass streaming stochastic K-armed bandits
unmapped: Arms arrive in an arbitrarily (adversarially) ordered read-only stream; algorithm may store at most M < K arms (identities and statistics) and can play only arms in memory
At most B passes over the stream; learner knows B and M
Stream order may change adversarially across passes (upper bound holds in that case)
settings.definition_quote: We assume a limited memory setting where the arms $\K$ are presented to the algorithm as an \emph{arbitrarily (or adversarially) ordered read-only stream}, and the algorithm is restricted to store the \emph{identities} and the corresponding \emph{statistics} of at most $M<K$ arms simultaneously while being allowed at most $B\geq 1$ passes over the stream.

settings.name_in_paper: Limited memory multi-pass streaming stochastic K-armed bandits (lower bound)
unmapped: Arms arrive in a read-only stream (fixed order across passes in the lower bound); algorithm may store at most M arms and can play only arms in memory
At most B passes over the stream
settings.definition_quote: We assume a limited memory setting where the arms $\K$ are presented to the algorithm as an \emph{arbitrarily (or adversarially) ordered read-only stream}, and the algorithm is restricted to store the \emph{identities} and the corresponding \emph{statistics} of at most $M<K$ arms simultaneously while being allowed at most $B\geq 1$ passes over the stream.

symbols.B: number of passes over the stream

conditions: B-pass algorithms using at most K/(8B(B+1) log e) words of memory
hard instances are Bernoulli with means 1/2 or 1/2+Delta_j (randomized distribution over instances)

source.label: thm:multi_pass_lower
source.quote: Given a time horizon $T$, a stream of $K$ arms, and passes $1\leq B < \log\log T$ over this stream, there exists a distribution over $K$-armed bandit instances such that any $B$-pass algorithm that uses at most $K\cdot(8B(B+1)\log e)^{-1}$ memory suffers $\Omega\paren{4^{-B}T^{2^B/(2^{B+1} - 1)}}$ regret in expectation.

results.notes: Regret defined via means, so pseudo-regret; expectation is over a prior on instances (Bayesian-style construction implying worst case). Follows from Lemma 3.2 with b=B (Lemma 3.2 not recorded separately). Algorithm class: memory-limited B-pass streaming algorithms.

symbols.B: number of passes over the stream

tuning: confidence radius sqrt(5 log T / n), c = 5

source.label: thm:main
source.quote: Given a time horizon $T$, a stream of $K$ arms, and number of passes $1\leq B< \log\log T$, there exists a $B$-pass algorithm that uses $O(1)$ words of memory, and with probability $1-1/\poly(T)$, achieves cumulative regret \[R_T \leq O\left(T^{\frac{2^B}{2^{B+1}-1}}\sqrt{KB\log T} \right).\]

results.notes: Holds w.p. 1-1/poly(T); proof also derives same bound in expectation. Holds under adversarial stream order changes across passes.

symbols.B: number of passes over the stream

source.label: thm:main
source.quote: Furthermore, supposing the arms $\K$ had mean rewards $\{\mu^*_j\}_{j\in\K}$, then given number of passes $1\leq B < \log T$, there exists a $B$-pass algorithm that uses $O(1)$ words of memory, and with probability $1-1/\poly(T)$, achieves a cumulative regret \[R_T \leq O\left(\sum_{j\in \S} \frac{T^{1/(B+1)} \log T + B \log\left((\Delta^*_j)^2T/\log T\right)}{\Delta^*_j}\right),\]

results.notes: Delta^*_j is the gap of arm j. Same bound also claimed in expectation in proof.
